capabilities.title: What the lifecycle is holding
capabilities.description: The open episode, the active task, the handover and checkpoint that resolve for this worktree and branch, each with its divergence label, the unresolved questions that refuse completion, and the record tallies. Selection is two-tiered and never repository-wide: a record from an unrelated worktree or branch is not offered, because a briefing that is quietly about somebody else is worse than none. Absence is reported as absence.

schema.description: No input.
schema.title: Empty

present.description:
Whether this checkout's lifecycle has ever run: a ledger line, a task, an episode or
a record. False in a fresh clone, which is not a fault.

It is not "the directory exists". Several things create that directory before
anything has been recorded in it, so a reader that took its presence for evidence
would be told the lifecycle had run in a checkout where it never had.

worktree.description: The worktree this answer is about. Every selection below is scoped to it.

head.description: The commit this checkout is on.

handover.description: The record the next worker would resume from, or `None` when nothing resolves here.

checkpoint.description: The newest progress note for this worktree and branch, or `None`.

blockers.description:
Unresolved questions on this branch. Every one refuses `finish --outcome completed`,
whichever task opened it.

tallies.description: How many records of each kind this checkout holds, against the policy's caps.

findings.description:
What a reader should know before trusting any of the above: a diverged record, a
foreign open session, a malformed file that was skipped. Empty is the good case.

schema.description: What the lifecycle of this checkout is holding.
schema.title: Continuity

worker.description: The worker identity, when one was supplied. Never inferred.

True when the open record here belongs to another checkout. Such a record is
reported and never treated as this checkout's episode.

outcome.description: Its typed outcome so far: `active`, `handed_over`, or a finished one.

created_at.description: When the record says it was written.

branch.description: The branch it was written on.

head.description: The commit it was written at.

working_tree.description: Whether the working tree was clean or dirty then.

matched.description: Which tier of the resolution rule matched.

divergence.description: How far its commit is from this one.

next_action.description:
The section a resuming worker acts on, when the record has one. A handover's `Next
Action`; empty for a record that carries no sections.

Record.description:
One durable record of the local half, as much of it as a reader needs to decide whether
to open the file.

oneOf.description: Same repository, same worktree, same branch.
Same repository, same branch, another worktree of it.

Match.description:
Which tier of the resolution rule matched. There is no third tier on purpose: a record
from an unrelated worktree or branch is never offered.

oneOf.description: Written at this commit. Trust it.
Git has moved forward since. Trust it, and expect some of it to be done.
The recorded commit is not an ancestor: history was rewritten. Trust git, not this.
Another branch or another worktree. This record is not about your work.
Git could not answer, so this process says so rather than guessing `exact`.

Divergence.description:
How far a record's recorded commit is from the commit this checkout is on.

The four words are the shell tool's, deliberately. A reader that met `advanced` from one
surface and `stale` from another would have to learn the same four facts twice.

capabilities.title: Performance counters
capabilities.description: The counters of this process: repository scans, index and registry builds, schema generations, projection builds, executions, handler invocations, cache hits, misses and evictions, and the phase timings, as they stand now.

schema.title: Empty

cache_misses.description: Executions of a cached capability that ran the handler.

The counters and phase totals of this process at one moment. Every value is a count
or a duration this process measured; none is written anywhere by hand.
